title: X9C-2 Policy Pilot Selection Decision

hard_rules: withCanonicalPolicyEnforcement can preserve existing behavior exactly
no high-risk mutation as first pilot

selection_rationale: After comprehensive audit of 31 routes using policy context or internalOnly pattern, found that all 4 policy-aware GET routes are ALREADY_CANONICAL_POLICY_SAFE. They currently use withCanonicalEnforcement with defensive policy fallback (ctx.policy ? hasInternalAccess(ctx.policy) : false). Migrating these routes to withCanonicalPolicyEnforcement WITHOUT adding requireInternalAccess or requirePolicyContext options would have zero behavioral impact. Adding options is not appropriate because these routes don't require/enforce internal access - they only use it for visibility filtering. Therefore, no new pilot routes can be selected that meet the criteria for meaningful migration.

reason_no_pilots: No routes meet pilot criteria. Routes already using safe canonical pattern don't benefit from migration. Routes using legacy pattern are deferred to later phases. Routes with service dependencies require X9C-3. Routes with governance dependencies require X9D.
what_this_means: X9C-2 is complete as a selection phase. The finding is that policy-aware GET routes are already properly canonicalized. No code changes needed for X9C-2. Next phase (X9C-3) will focus on service-layer refactoring where needed.
next_step_if_no_pilots: Proceed to X9C-3 readiness planning without X9C-2 pilots. Service refactoring will be the main X9C-3 work, not route migration.

final_determination: ZERO pilots selected. All policy-aware GET routes are already in correct canonical pattern. X9C-2 phase confirms this assessment. No code changes will occur in X9C-2. Migration roadmap shifts focus to X9C-3 (service refactoring) and X9D (workspace/role design) as identified blockers are resolved.
